tweet.text:
Run Kimi K3 locally with Unsloth!

Kimi K3 is the strongest open-weight model available right now. 2.8 trillion total parameters, 104B active per token, 1 million token context window, and thinking-only inference with native vision.

The full precision model needs 1.56 TB of RAM and VRAM combined. That's not realistic for almost anyone.

Unsloth's Dynamic 1-bit GGUF brings the smallest version down to 594 GB on disk. A 62% reduction from full precision. But it still needs at least 610 GB of total memory (RAM + VRAM, or unified memory) to run. Realistically this means an NVIDIA DGX Station or a Mac Studio connected to additional RAM. This is not a consumer setup.

The quality tradeoff at 1-bit: 78.9% top-1 accuracy against the full precision model. Perplexity of 2.58. Surprisingly usable for a 1-bit quant.

Worth noting: other community quants at similar sizes perform far worse. A 618 GB community 1-bit quant reaches perplexity of 54.56 compared to Unsloth's 2.58 at 594 GB - 21x worse. Dynamic quantization with proper calibration makes the difference.

If you have more headroom, Dynamic 2-bit at 861 GB reaches 90% top-1 accuracy. Q8 lossless sits at 1.56 TB - essentially full precision.

Runs via llama.cpp or Unsloth Studio on macOS, Windows, and Linux. Thinking effort is configurable: low, high, or max. Preserve thinking is always on by default.

Key details:

• Smallest quant: 594 GB disk, 610 GB RAM required (Dynamic 1-bit)
• Dynamic 2-bit: 861 GB disk, 880 GB RAM, 90% top-1 accuracy
• Full precision: 1.56 TB disk and RAM
• 78.9% top-1 accuracy at 1-bit vs 21x worse perplexity from community quants
• Thinking-only model, preserve thinking always enabled
• Native vision support
• Runs via llama.cpp or Unsloth Studio

I've shared the Unsloth guide in the replies!
